finding: The false-typical (FT) cell -- confident, fluent, in-distribution falsehood -- is intrinsically hard to construct cleanly. Neither synthetic swaps nor natural-error harvesting produce it without an artifact or at usable yield.

builds.lesson: FT starved (78); FA dominates. Random swaps make odd (high-ppl) lies.

builds.generation: frequency-aware swaps (common vs rare object) + C3 subword matching
builds.lesson: FT still starved: perplexity ENCODES TRUTH, so a low-ppl false item barely exists (the LM scores false statements high-ppl because it knows they are false).

Frequency axis SOLVES cell coverage (FT 72->540) -- but swaps leave a PERSISTENT hidden-state edit signature the canary detects (~0.67), even with edited-orthogonal-to-truth held at generation (0.505/0.559).
builds.correction: At full n=2164 the edit-canary CI includes 0.50 -> the 0.67 at 134/cell was small-n noise; swaps do NOT leave a significant edit signature. Fragmentation leak (0.625, CI excludes 0.50) is real but was measured WITHOUT the C3 subword control on the canary set.

examples: Santarem is a city in Portugal.
Oyster Bay is a city in New Zealand.
As Sib is a city in Iraq.
Al Mubarraz is a city in Oman.
Altamira is a city in Mexico.
harvest.lesson: No edit signature (real outputs), but 2.5% yield and obscure-skewed -> FT (common-entity confident error) yield ~= 0. Some errors ambiguous (Santarem is in both Portugal and Brazil).

conclusion: Across three synthetic builds and a natural-error harvest, the FT cell cannot be populated cleanly and at scale: swaps contaminate hidden states with an edit signature; harvesting yields too few, obscure-skewed errors. This is the MIRAGE thesis in its strongest form -- the one off-diagonal cell that would expose the truth-vs-typicality confound is the cell that is intrinsically hard to construct, which is precisely why internal-state probes are only ever validated on the diagonal.
